paragraphs: nCase Technologies sells nCase Lite, a silicone carry case that holds one dose of naloxone nasal spray. Naloxone nasal spray is not included with the case. The case clips to keys, bags, or belts, and a QR sticker on it links to naloxone administration instructions. The case is compatible with emergency nasal sprays including naloxone, NARCAN, neffy, and VALTOCO.

Smaller orders go through the website, and bulk pricing is tiered by unit volume. Bulk purchasing is offered for public health programs, universities, hospitals, and other organizations. Discounts go to nonprofits, public health departments, government agencies, and first responder teams. Accepted payment methods include credit card, purchase orders, ACH, and wire transfer, with Net 30 terms for health departments and government agencies.

nCase was founded by Dani Wilder and Matt Bitner-Glindzicz, whose backgrounds are in healthcare, research, and mechanical design. The company states that the case is not a medical device and is not regulated by the FDA.

quote.text: nCase is a protective carrying case to carry your naloxone.
